'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**Around 40 people are killed by an American [[cruise missile]] strike targeting [[al-Qaeda]]-linked militants at a [[Huras al-Din]] base in Syria's rebel-held [[Idlib Governorate]], where the Syrian government earlier began a unilateral ceasefire. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-49538528 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-syria/u-s-forces-strike-syrian-al-qaeda-facility-defense-department-idUSKCN1VL0LA (Reuters)]
*[[2018–19 Gaza border protests]]
**The [[Hamas]]-run Health Ministry of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] says a 25-year-old man died in hospital there today after being struck by an [[Israel]]i bullet during protests at the Gazan-Israeli border yesterday. It further says Israeli soldiers wounded 42 protesters. Israel says [[Palestinians]] threw grenades at the fence, damaging a vehicle and injuring a soldier. [https://news.yahoo.com/officials-gaza-man-dies-wounds-102211746.html (Yahoo!)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban]] fighters storm [[Kunduz]] city, apparently killing three civilians and dozens of soldiers. A suicide bomber kills ten municipal police. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-49536374 (BBC News)] [https://www.tolonews.com/afghanistan/blast-kunduz-city-leaves-10-dead-several-wounded (Tolo News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires]]
**[[Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Brazil)|Foreign Minister]] [[Ernesto Araújo]] states that the fires have mostly been extinguished. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/08/31/world/fires-amazon-extinguished-brazil-says/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[2019 Alta helicopter crash]]
**An [[Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil|Airbus AS350]] helicopter crashes in northern [[Norway]], killing all five Norwegian passengers and the [[Sweden|Swedish]] pilot. [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/article/2001340326/six-die-in-helicopter-crash-in-norway (''Standard'')]
*An explosion followed by a fire at a chemical factory in [[Dhule]], [[India]] kills at least 12 and injures at least 58. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/08/31/india/india-dhule-chemical-factory-explosion-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Eastern equine encephalitis]]
**The [[Maine]] health department confirms a horse in [[York County, Maine|York County]] has tested positive for the rare, deadly, [[Zoonosis|potentially transferable to humans]], mosquito-borne viral disease [[Eastern equine encephalitis]]. Earlier this week, an infected 14-year-old [[Michigan]] girl was hospitalized in serious condition, and [[Ohio]] officials confirmed an [[Ashtabula County, Ohio|Ashtabula County]] horse also tested positive.  Neither of the horses were [[Eastern equine encephalitis#Prevention|vaccinated]] against EEE. [https://www.newsweek.com/eee-virus-identified-maine-1457097 (''Newsweek'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2019/08/28/eastern-equine-encephalitis-rare-virus-hospitalizes-michigan-teen/2147508001/ (''USA Today'')] [https://thehorse.com/178245/eastern-equine-encephalomyelitis-confirmed-in-ohio-horse/ (''The Horse'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[India]] releases the final version of the [[National Register of Citizens of India|National Register of Citizens]] for the state of [[Assam]]. Up to 1.9 million residents risk losing their [[Indian nationality law|citizenship]] if they are not on the list and can not prove their residency. The move is criticized for disproportionately affecting the local [[Bengalis|Bengali]] community. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-49520593 (BBC News)] 
*[[Brexit]]
**Thousands of people join protests across the [[United Kingdom]] against the suspension of the [[UK Parliament]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2019/aug/31/brexit-stopthecoup-protests-uk-proroguing (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Amazon rainforest wildfires|Amazon rainforest wildfires]]
**The [[Brazilian Institute of Environment and Renewable Natural Resources]] (IBAMA) raids an illegal wildcat miners' site in the state of [[Pará]] as the country resumes environmental policing of the [[Amazon rainforest|rainforest]]. The suspects escape following a [[Shootout|firefight]]. [https://nypost.com/2019/08/31/brazil-ramps-up-environmental-policing-amid-outrage-over-amazon-fires/ (''New York Post'']
*[[Midland–Odessa shootings]]
**At least seven people are killed and 21 others wounded in a mass shooting in [[West Texas]], between the cities of [[Midland, Texas|Midland]] and [[Odessa, Texas|Odessa]]. The shooter is shot and killed in Odessa. Police continue to investigate for other possible suspects. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49540160 (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2019/08/31/us/odessa-texas-active-shooter/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-texas-shooting/five-killed-including-shooter-around-21-injured-in-texas-shooting-police-media-idUSKCN1VL0SP (Reuters)] [https://www.massshootingtracker.org/data (MST)]
*[[2016 Interstate 10 tour bus crash]]
**A truck driver involved in the accident, which killed thirteen when two vehicles collided in [[California]], pleads guilty to 42 crimes including [[vehicular manslaughter]]. The sleep-deprived driver fell asleep during a temporary halt to traffic; when traffic moved off again he remained stationary and the bus ran into the rear of his vehicle. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/trucker-pleads-guilty-california-crash-killed-13-65320848 (ABC News)]
*[[2019 Lyon stabbings]]
**An [[Afghanistan|Afghan citizen]] stabs nine in [[Lyon]], France, killing a 19-year-old. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/08/31/europe/france-villeurbanne-knife-attack/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2019 Spa-Francorchamps FIA Formula 2 round]]
**[[Formula 2]] racing driver [[Anthoine Hubert]] dies in a collision during a race at the [[Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps]] in [[Belgium]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/aug/31/spa-f2-race-abandoned-antoine-hubert-juan-manuel-correa-crash (''The Guardian'')]
